sections.description:
THE PUNJAB PROHIBITION AND RESTRICTION OF LIQUOR RULES, 1949
THE PUNJAB
PROHIBITION AND RESTRICTION OF LIQUOR RULES, 1949
[Gaz. 28th
September, 1949]
No. 1503-E & T, 26th
September, 1949.--In exercise of the powers conferred by clause (1) of
sub-section (2) of Section 58 of the Punjab Excise Act, 1914, added by the
Punjab Excise (Amendment) Act, 1949, sub section (4) of Section 24 ibid, and
all other powers enabling him in this behalf and in pursuance of Punjab
Government Notification No. 1407-E & T, dated the 13th September 1949, the
Governor of Punjab is pleased to make the following rules:‑
1. (i) These rules may be
called the Punjab Prohibition and Restriction of Liquor Rules, 1949.
(ii) The term
"licensed druggist', "Licensed chemist", "Medical
practitioner" and "prescription" shall mutatis mutandis have the
same meanings as are assigned to them in the "Punjab Manufactured Drugs
Rules" notified under Punjab Government Notification No. 6400-E & S,
dated the 30th November 1932.
(ii) (a)
"Restaurant" means any place to which the public is admitted for
consumption of food or drink for consideration.
(iii) "Approved
hotel" shall include an hotel licensed under the Excise Act or such other
hotel as has been approved by the Excise Commissioners for the purposes of
these rules.
(iv) "Financial
year" shall mean the period from 1st April to the 31st March inclusive.
(v) "Resident
Excise Sub-Inspector' shall mean an Excise Sub-Inspector posted for the time
being at an hotel licensed under the Punjab Excise Act of 1914.
(vi) "Assistant
Excise and Taxation Officer" or "Excise and Taxation Officer"
shall mean an officer appointed as such by the Provincial Government.
(vii) "Deputy
Director, Excise and Taxation" shall mean an officer appointed as such by
the Provincial Government.
2. (i) In addition to
other permits provided for under the Punjab Excise Act, 1914, or the Rules made
thereunder the permits in forms Pr. II, Pr. IV, Pr. V, Pr. VII, Pr. VIII and
Pr. IX appended to these rules may be granted or renewed subject to the
provisions of these rules by the authorities mentioned against each form of
permit in the following tables:‑
Table
(ii) The authorities subordinate
to the Excise Commissioner as empowered to grant or renew permits shall
exercise these powers subject to the control of the Excise Commissioner.
(iii) All or any of the powers of
Excise and Taxation Officer or Assistant Excise and Taxation Officer, specified
above, may be exercised by the Deputy Excise and Taxation Commissioner or
Excise Commissioner.
3. An Application for
grant of a permit under these rules shall be made in writing and, so far as
possible, shall give:
(i) in the case
of an individual;
(a)
Name and address of the applicant.
(b) "Father's
name.
(c) Age.
(d) Identification
mark.
(e) Religion.
(f) Profession
or trade.
(g) Units of
liquor in poss6sion on the date of making the application.
(h) Number of
units required per mensum or on the specified occasion only; and
(ii) in the case
of a non-proprietary club or a mess or a canteen or other similar institution;
(a) Name and
description of the non-proprietary club/mess/canteen/or similar institution.
(b) Locality.
(c) District.
(d) Number of
Muslim and non-Muslim members separately.
(e) Treasury
voucher number in token of payment of permit fee.
Application for grant of permits
in form Pr. II and Pr. V may be made in the form Pr. I and applications for
grant of permits in form Pr. IV may be made in form Pr. III.
4. (1) An application for
the grant of a permit under these rules shall be made within a reasonable time
before the date from which it is proposed to be availed of.
(2) The application for the
renewal of a permit in form Pr. IV, Pr. VIII or Pr. VIII shall be made at least
30 days before the date of its expiry provided that the authority competent to
renew it may, at its discretion, entertain an application made later.
5. No permit shall be
transferable.

permit on its expiry
